question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{n-4{n}^{6}}{3{n}^{2}-1}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
The dominant term in the denominator is $3{n}^{2},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{n-4{n}^{6}}{3{n}^{2}-1} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{n}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{4{n}^{6}}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{1}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{n}-4{n}^{4})}{(3-\frac{1}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{0-4{n}^{4}}{3-0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(-\frac{4}{3}{n}^{4}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.
